question.leadin: A 1950s government led by this party saw Minister of Housing Harold Macmillan lead a construction boom and Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden support a coup d'etat in Iran.
question.text: Name this British political party, which defeated the Labour Party of Clement Attlee in 1951 elections.
question.clue: A foreign secretary from this party issued a statement supporting a "national home" in an Ottoman area.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about English monarchs.
swap.text: George V and Elizabeth II are of this ruling house.
swap.clue: Considered one of the automotive capitals of Canada, this city lies at one end of the Ambassador Bridge across the Detroit River from Detroit.

question.text: This man was the first Prime Minister of Canada. He served in two separate terms after resigning due to the Pacific Railway Scandal, which saw Tory politicians bribed to give out prime rail routes.
question.clue: In the Great Coalition, this man joined George-Etienne Cartier and George Brown at the Charlottetown Conference to push for confederation.

swap.leadin: Phrases like "sick animal," "trained seal," "evil genius," "does not have a spine," and "devoid of honour" are listed as unparliamentary language in a book titled for Arthur Beauchesne, a clerk of this body.
swap.text: Name this lower house of Canadian Parliament, which shares its name with the house in the UK contrasted with the House of Lords.
swap.clue: The ability of wealthy men to purchase housing and instill tenants willing to vote as they wished, along with the outsized representation possible in districts with a tiny number of residents, led to reform of this body in 1832.

question.text: This 1774 act allowed the free practice of Catholicism in its namesake colony, and also defined the boundary for that colony.
question.clue: This act was one of the intolerable acts. It allowed freedom of religion in Canada and granted the namesake colony land west of the Appalachian.

swap.text: This Canadian unifying event consisted of three different uprisings including the Patriot War. This event led to the merger of Lower and Upper Canada into a single government and to the issuing of the Durham report.
swap.clue: This series of Canadian revolts which saw the Patriote movement fight British troops at Sainte-Charles and Sainte Eustache during the namesake year.

question.leadin: This conflict began after the kidnapping of diplomat James Cross.
question.text: Name this period of unrest initiated by the Front de Liberation Quebec in 1970.
question.clue: Robert Bourassa appeared on television five minutes prior to a deadline in this event stating that his government would not negotiate, resulting in the retaliatory execution of Pierre LaPorte, who had been kidnapped along with James Cross.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a major North American oil exporter.
swap.text: Louis Riel led this mixed-race ethnic group in a failed rebellion against the Canadian government in 1885.
swap.clue: Garnet Wolseley led a namesake expedition to confront these people in 1870.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Manitoba schools question of the 1890s.
question.text: The Manitoba Schools Question allowed this man to defeat Charles Tupper in the 1896 federal election. This man was Canada's first French-speaking prime minister.
question.clue: This replacement of Charles Tupper created his nation's "tin pot" navy when he signed the Naval Service Bill.

swap.text: Some Haudenosaunee believe "Iroquois" to be derived from the language of this tribe. This tribe fought the Haudenosaunee in the Beaver Wars and name a lake whose Manitoulin Island was sacred to the Anishinaabe.
swap.clue: Many of these people banded together with the related "Tobacco People," or Petun, after a 1648 attack that killed the Jesuit Jean de Brebeuf.

question.text: Under King, Canada saw a 1926 constitutional crisis when Julian Byng, who held this office, refused King's request to dissolve Parliament and hold new elections. This office represents the English monarchy in Canada.
question.clue: In 1952, Vincent Massey became the first holder of this position to not be a member of the peerage.

swap.leadin: This man was forced to resign by the Pacific Scandal in 1873 before returning to the same position five years later after beating Alexander Mackenzie in the 1878 election.
swap.text: Name this Conservative party member who served as the first prime minister of Canada.
swap.clue: This first Prime Minister of Canada who resigned for a short time after the Pacific Scandal.

question.leadin: This man replaced Louis Saint Laurent as Prime Minister, ending 22 years of Liberal rule.
question.text: Name this Canadian prime minister who passed the Canadian Bill of Rights in 1960. He cancelled the Avro Arrow project after agreeing to accept Bomarc nuclear missiles from the United States.
question.clue: He also cancelled the Avro Arrow program, halting production of fighter jets in his country, when he signed NORAD with the US. Raised in Saskatchewan, he passed his country's Bill of Rights, and presided over the opening of the St. Lawrence Seaway.

swap.text: The Patriotes' 1837 rebellion against British rule occurred in this North American colony. This colony, which comprised present-day Quebec, was later unified with an oppositely named colony corresponding to Ontario.

question.leadin: Jean Chretien ("crate-YENN") led this party to a strong majority in the 1993 Canadian federal election.
question.text: Name this centrist Canadian political party led from 1968 to 1984 by Pierre Trudeau.
question.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Canada [or Parti libéral du Canada]
question.clue: A request to dissolve parliament by a leader of this party was refused by Governor-General Julian Byng in 1926.

swap.leadin: This leader reclassified thousands of orphans as mentally ill in order to claim extra federal subsidies for their care, leading to abuse of children in insane asylums on a massive scale.
swap.text: Name this Quebecois leader who implemented a set of conservative policies called the Great Darkness before his Union Nationale Party was deposed in 1959.
swap.clue: The church opposed Laurier with the slogan "Heaven is blue, hell is red," which was later taken up by this Premier of Quebec. This conservative passed the Padlock Law and presided over a period called "The Great Darkness."

question.leadin: Answer the following about strained racial relations in Canadian history.
question.text: This militantly anti-English group's killing of Pierre Laporte in 1970 led to the October Crisis, in which Pierre Trudeau deployed military forces to restore order.
question.answerHtml: FLQ [or Front de libération du Québec; or Quebec Liberation Front]
question.clue: The (+) South Shore Gang was a subgroup of this organization, members of which kidnapped James Cross and Pierre Laporte in an action that prompted Pierre Trudeau to invoke the War Measures Act.

swap.text: During Mulroney's tenure as Prime Minister, he signed the Meech Lake Accords with this man, the Premier of Quebec.

question.text: The Popham settlement was a direct reaction to the St. Croix settlement of 1604, briefly capital of this French New World territory that notionally spanned the Bay of Fundy, Nova Scotia, and the Atlantic Coast of Canada.
question.clue: This colony had its southern border with colonial Maine established along the Kennebec River.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about formative events of Canada, FTPE.
swap.text: This conference in Prince Edward Island saw delegates from four colonies, including New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, spend a week discussing the formation of a Canadian confederation.
swap.clue: A month after this meeting, a similar meeting was held in the mainland part of the country that this meeting occurred in. One of the attendees at this event became the first prime minister of the country this meeting occurred in, John Macdonald.
